title: Growth of the Batagay (Batagaika) megaslump
summary: The Batagay megaslump in the Yana Uplands of Yakutia, a retrogressive permafrost thaw slump, was first recognised on satellite imagery of 1991, after forming from a hillside ravine. By 2023 it covered 87.6 hectares, the largest megaslump on Earth, and was losing about one million cubic metres of ice and sediment a year.

uncertainty.note: Kizyakov et al. (2024): the slump formed in the 1970s, its initiation "most likely some time between 1980 and 1991", first recognised on satellite imagery of 1991; area measured through 2023. Years 1970-2023 span formation to the latest measurement.
